description: We are team solving the challenge Planet X and SPHEREx. We are enthusiastic and exited to solve this challenge
summary: Snapspace is a web-based tool which allows users to view SPHEREx imagery based off of IRSA image data via SIA v2 based on provided coordinates (right ascension and declination). It sports several features, such as displaying photometry graphs of the area within the image that a user may click on, displaying metadata such as flags for contamination, viewing the image frames spliced together with adjustable rate of frame change, as well as adjustable FOV and configurable color options, such as viewing the frames in RGB with 102 infrared bands. Additionally, the coordinates can be entered from the URL, allowing for embedding within other sites and projects.
details:
To start the project, we started looking for suitable APIs which would be able to fetch the needed images. The goal was for the program to be able to fetch the APIs based on the coordinates of a segment of the sky (right ascension & declination). We also expected the API will need some sort of time period for input. For this, we expected to be able to create a function within the program to find the oldest record of the image, with its respective time period, and increment it accordingly until it reaches the latest. The program may need to load each image before displaying it on the UI, and then the app would essentially display them sequentially in a speed such that it looks like a timelapse. A nice feature to have would be a slider in the UI by which this speed is controlled. This would be helpful for closer and more careful examination of details in the image some may find relevant.

Given the tool should be web-based, we reasoned the project should be programmed in Javascript, among other web development frameworks. For the program itself, the outline seemed relatively simple: take input of coordinates, use the API to fetch the oldest image from the first available image to the last, save them to an array, use a for loop to increment the index over a configurable delay and output to UI.

With that in mind, we had started development. In terms of an API, we had found that to implement fetching imagery into the project, the way to do it was to use IRSA image data which would be accessed through the SIA v2 interface. For developing the project as a whole, given its complexity, it was found best to utilize the assistance of AI to work on the project. After thoroughly prompting according to our directives, we were able to create what we consider a successful product. We were then able to host the website with the same AI tool which assisted us with programming the project.

The project, which can be found at this URL, is capable of adjustable FOV and framerate, implementing 102 infrared bands into the image’s color range, flagging frames for potential contamination, displaying graphs of spectra, among other features. Additionally coordinate parameters are adjustable from the URL. This makes it convenient for those who may wish to externally use or embed this project. The project’s name, Snapspace, was derived from a play on the words “snapshot” and “space”. Similarly, the logo of it is inspired by that of Snapchat’s and the NASA logo, employing a play on the word “snapchat” with themes of space, hence signifying “Snapspace”.
